Table that contains the main information and properties of the coadded images. These images have been created combining the individual processed science images for each filter. The detection and the object properties contained in the other tables have been computed from these images.
Table that contains all the calibration data of the tiles. For each tile, this table contains the zero point and error obtained using different calibration methods.

Table that contains the main parameters of the astronomical objects detected in the images. The object detection and aperture definition is performed in a reference band ('rSDSS') and the measurements are done in each filter using SExtractor (Dual Mode). Array columns (type[]) contains measures for each filter (NULL if the image in the filter is not available). Enumeration 'jplus' can be used to refer filter positions in the array. Flux data is adjusted by the image Zero Point and is in 10<sup>-30</sup>erg/s/cm<sup>2</sup>/Hz units.

Only the counterpart with lower quality is listed in this table. Array columns (type[]) contains measures for each filter (NULL if not available yet). Enumeration 'jplus' can be used to refer filter positions in the array. Flux data is adjusted by the image Zero Point and is in 10<sup>-30</sup>erg/s/cm<sup>2</sup>/Hz units.

Table that contains the available variability information of the sources detected in Dual Mode after a cross-match with the Known_Variables catalogue (2015, restricted access).

Table that contains the B-V color excess due to Milky Way dust at the position of the sources. The integrated E(B-V), this is, estimated at infinity, is provided and was estimated from the Schlafly & Finkbeiner (2011) recalibration of the Schlegel, Finkbeiner & Davis (1998) infrared-based (COBE/DIRBE and IRAS/ISSA) dust map. Objects are identified by tile_id and number columns. The E(B-V) is computed for those objects in dual mode tables.

Table that contains the photometric redshifts of the astronomical objects obtained with the LePhare software (Arnouts & Ilbert 2011).
The photometric redshifts are computed by SED-fitting with galaxy templates using a redshift search range from z=0 to z=1 in steps of dz=0.005. Therefore, the values provided are only meaningful for sources that happen to be galaxies at z < 1. A magnitude cut r_AUTO < 22 was applied. Fainter J-PLUS sources do not have an entry in this table. Raw redshift probability distribution functions (PDF) from LePhare have been calibrated and stored as quantiles of the cumulative PDF. All summary statistics provided are measured from the calibrated PDF. The quantiles of the cumulative PDF are stored in a compressed form in the COLDPRESS_PDF column. To extract the full PDF from it, here you have the software and instructions.
The photometric information in tables FNuDualObj and DuplicatedFNuDualObj has been used as input.
Updated 6th July 2026: New columns added: Z_MEDIAN_ERR and ODDS_MEDIAN.

Table that contains the photometric redshifts of the astronomical objects obtained with the LeMoNNADE software (Hernán-Caballero et al., in prep.). The photometric redshifts are computed by a neural network trained on a large sample of J-PLUS sources with spectroscopic redshifts from DESI, SDSS, HectoMAP and HETDEX.

Two separated models are trained for binary classification (star/extragalactic) and photometric redshifts for extragalactic sources. The classification (P_STAR) and redshifts are predicted based solely on the photometry of J-PLUS and do not rely on any morphological parameters or external source classification. J-PLUS sources that are fainter than r=22 or saturated in the g, r, or i bands do not have an entry in this table.

Photometric redshifts probability density functions (PDFs) are computed for all the sources in the table regardless of their P_STAR value. The PDFs and the point estimates derived from them are conditional to the source being extragalactic (galaxy or QSO). The full PDF is provided (in a compressed form) in the COLDPRESS_PDF column. To extract the full PDF from it, here you have the software and instructions.

The photometric information in tables FNuDualObj and DuplicatedFNuDualObj has been used as input.

Updated 6th July 2026: New columns added: Z_MEDIAN_ERR and ODDS_MEDIAN.
